description: next/ v4 — WMS stock levels (Quant) aligned to SMProfile-Quant (next/). Provides, over the it-edge/BUSINESS path, a business.* stream (entity_type=quant), keyed on the UPSTREAM column 'quant_id' (response.idProperty is an upstream RESPONSE FIELD name, not the smAttribute 'quant_no' it maps to — 2.0.0 named the smAttribute there, so every one of the 500 rows resolved to a null primary key and the source emitted nothing at all; see ci/lint-source-keys.mjs). article_ref + blocked ('gesperrt' column) + quantity ('menge' column) drive the cross-domain deviation material_unavailable: an active OperationsResponse needs article_ref X, sum(free WMS stock X | blocked==0) == 0 -> multi_source discrepancy. full_refresh: delivers the current stock list per poll (no timestamp diff). CAPT-RETRACT 2026-08-18 - VERDICT: THIS SOURCE CANNOT AND MUST NOT BE MADE TO RETRACT BY PAGINATION, and polling.paginate is deliberately NOT set. It IS live (in osf-it-edge-wms SOURCE_IDS) and it-edge (DATA-7) refuses its delete/tombstone pass every 60 s with reason unpaginated_full_refresh - 28 refusals in a measured 30-minute window. THE REFUSAL IS SAVING US. Measured from the refusal lines themselves: seenCount 500, trackedCount 229,054 and RISING (229,120 one minute later), wouldHaveRetracted 228,554. erp.stock_quants holds 3,674,874 rows, ALL distinct quant_id, spanning 2026-07-17 to now and growing 56,011-87,831 rows/day. The endpoint default page is 500 rows ordered by updated_at DESC, so what it-edge sees per poll is an EIGHT-MINUTE SLIVER of a 32-day ledger: the 500 rows returned spanned 16:32:10Z to 16:40:05Z, and two calls 3 s apart shared only 486 of 500. 3,674,491 rows lie OUTSIDE that window and STILL EXIST upstream - so every one of the 228,554 rows it-edge wanted to retract is a LIVE row, and declaring paginate on the assumption that absence means deletion would have been a mass deletion, not a repair. WHY PAGINATION IS THE WRONG MECHANISM HERE, on three independent counts. (1) UNAFFORDABLE: at the server measured hard cap of 5000 rows per request that is 735 requests per poll, every 60 s, at a measured 346 bytes/row = about 1.27 GB per poll = about 21 MB/s sustained against an already overloaded .154. (2) INCONSISTENT: the table grows about 1.3 rows/s, so the population changes while you page it and a page-through can never be a consistent snapshot. (3) UNNECESSARY, and this is the decisive one - THE UPSTREAM NEVER DELETES A QUANT. Consumption sets qty_on_hand to 0 and KEEPS the row: 242,163 zero-qty rows are present, the oldest from 2026-07-17T17:26:41Z. There is no upstream deletion for a retraction to propagate, so cannot-retract is not a defect of this source - it is the correct behaviour, and DATA-7 failing closed is doing exactly its job. THE ACTUAL DEFECT SITS UPSTREAM OF RETRACTION AND IT IS WORSE: this descriptor models an append-only 3.67M-row event LEDGER as a full_refresh stock SNAPSHOT with batchSize 1000. quant_id is not a stable stock identity - it embeds a mint timestamp and its producer (e.g. Q-press-02-20260818163317-_V4_BG-FL-002) - so every production event mints a NEW key. The consequence is measurable in the graph: 378,430 :Quant nodes in the KG, which is neither the upstream population (3,674,874) nor the current stock, but an arbitrary accumulation of eight-minute slivers. PROPOSAL, deliberately NOT applied here because a source already in SOURCE_IDS must not be re-modelled by a descriptor edit alone: either (a) give the WMS a bounded CURRENT-STOCK projection to poll - aggregate to (lager_nr, lagerplatz_id, artikel_nr, charge_nr) with qty > 0, which is the entity SMProfile-Quant actually describes and is small enough to page completely - or (b) reclassify this feed as what it is, an append-only event stream on a timestamp delta (changeDetection timestamp plus timestampQueryParam), which never claims a full population and therefore never asks DATA-7 for a retraction it cannot license. Until one of those is decided, the honest state of this source is INGEST-ONLY, and the 60-second DATA-7 refusal is the correct outcome rather than a bug to silence.
